questions.q: How do standard Snowflake views compare to standard SQL Server views?
options: They work the same way — a stored query computed at read time, with no data of its own
Snowflake views always physically store their query results
Snowflake has no concept of views at all
Snowflake views require a different query language than the underlying tables
questions.explain: Standard views need no adjustment coming from T-SQL — Snowflake also adds secure views and materialized views as extensions, but the basic concept is identical.

questions.q: Which Snowflake table persistence type has no direct SQL Server equivalent?
options: Transient tables
Permanent tables
Temporary tables
All three have direct SQL Server equivalents
questions.explain: SQL Server has permanent tables and #temp tables, but nothing matching Snowflake's transient table type — same durability as permanent, but without a Fail-safe period.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a permanent table and a transient table in Snowflake?
options: Transient tables have no Fail-safe period and minimal Time Travel, making them cheaper to store
Transient tables cannot be queried by more than one user
Transient tables are automatically dropped after 24 hours
Permanent tables cannot use Time Travel at all
questions.explain: Both persist until dropped and are visible to anyone with access, but transient tables skip the 7-day Fail-safe recovery window that permanent tables get, saving storage cost.

questions.q: What happens to a temporary table when the session that created it ends?
options: It is automatically dropped — no DROP TABLE statement is needed
It becomes a permanent table automatically
It remains visible to all other sessions indefinitely
It is converted into a view
questions.explain: Temporary tables are scoped to the creating session and are invisible to other sessions; they're dropped automatically the moment that session ends.

questions.q: Why would you mark a staging table as TRANSIENT instead of leaving it as the default permanent type?
options: Staging data is usually reproducible by reloading from the source, so the Fail-safe recovery window isn't needed and skipping it saves storage cost
Transient tables run queries faster than permanent tables
Permanent tables cannot be used in ELT pipelines
Transient is required for any table referenced by a view
questions.explain: Since staging/intermediate pipeline data can typically be reloaded if something goes wrong, paying for the extra Fail-safe recovery window that permanent tables carry is usually unnecessary cost.
